# pushward_org_sso_connection (Resource)

The organization's single sign-on connection, OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0. Enterprise plan only; declare at most one.

Only an owner sets it up or changes its identity provider (the protocol, the OIDC issuer or client_id, the SAML entity ID, SSO URL or signing certificates), and an org admin key acts as an admin, so PushWard refuses those changes from Terraform with a 403. An owner sets it up in the [PushWard console](https://console.pushward.app); then `terraform import` brings it in, and Terraform manages `enabled` and `require_sso`, and can roll the OIDC client secret or save the same SAML metadata again. Creating the resource while the connection already exists with the same identity provider adopts it the same way.

PushWard never returns the OIDC client secret. Terraform sends it when it changes, and when the connection is created or its provider changes, and does not notice a secret changed in the console. `client_secret_wo` (Terraform 1.11 or newer) keeps it out of the plan and the state, and is the form to prefer. The SAML metadata is sent the same way: a change that leaves it alone keeps the stored identity provider and asks it nothing, so `enabled` and `require_sso` can be turned off while the metadata URL is down. With neither metadata attribute (`saml = {}`) none is ever sent, and Terraform manages an existing SAML connection's `enabled` and `require_sso` only: also one set up from an uploaded document, or whose metadata URL already lists the next certificate.

Turning it on needs a verified domain, so in the apply that verifies one, make it `depends_on` the `pushward_org_domain_verification`. That verification stays in the state, also when the domain lapses back to `pending`, so later changes do not wait for it; one Terraform has to create again (its domain was removed or replaced) holds them up until it is through or times out. To change the connection first, say to turn `require_sso` off, take the `depends_on` out for that apply: `-target` brings the dependencies along. While no domain is verified, PushWard refuses `enabled = true`.

Destroying it removes the connection; the console sessions it signed in stay valid until they expire.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An owner sets the connection up in the PushWard console and it is imported
# (see below). Terraform then turns it on and rolls the client secret.
resource "pushward_org_sso_connection" "this" {
  protocol    = "oidc"
  enabled     = true
  require_sso = true

  oidc = {
    issuer    = "https://login.example.com"
    client_id = "pushward"

    # Never stored in the plan or state. Bump the version to send a rolled
    # secret.
    client_secret_wo         = var.sso_client_secret
    client_secret_wo_version = 1
  }

  # Turning it on needs a verified domain. Once one is verified this holds a
  # change up only while Terraform verifies a domain again after it was
  # removed or replaced; to change the connection first (say, turn
  # require_sso off), take this line out for that apply.
  depends_on = [pushward_org_domain_verification.example]
}

variable "sso_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

# A SAML 2.0 connection takes the identity provider's metadata instead, or
# none at all: saml = {} keeps what the owner saved, and Terraform manages the
# switches only.
#
#   protocol = "saml"
#   saml = {
#     idp_metadata_url = "https://login.example.com/saml/metadata"
#   }
```

## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether people sign in with it. Turning it on needs a verified domain.
- `protocol` (String) `oidc` or `saml`, with the block of the same name. Switching it takes an owner.

### Optional

- `oidc` (Attributes) The OpenID Connect identity provider, with protocol `oidc`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--oidc))
- `require_sso` (Boolean) Console sessions of members other than owners must have signed in with it. Owners are exempt, so an identity provider outage cannot lock the organization out. Defaults to `false`.
- `saml` (Attributes) The SAML 2.0 identity provider's metadata, with protocol `saml`: `idp_metadata_xml` or `idp_metadata_url`, or neither to keep the identity provider PushWard has stored. Metadata with another entity ID, SSO URL or other signing certificates takes an owner. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--saml))

### Read-Only

- `acs_url` (String) The assertion consumer service URL (HTTP-POST) to register at a SAML identity provider.
- `id` (String) The organization id.
- `idp_certificate_fingerprints` (List of String) The SHA-256 fingerprints of the SAML identity provider's signing certificates, colon-separated upper case hex.
- `idp_entity_id` (String) The SAML identity provider's entity ID, from its metadata.
- `org_id` (String) The organization the resource belongs to, that of the provider's org admin key when the resource was created or imported. An org admin key of another organization is an error, not a plan that creates the resource again there.
- `redirect_uri` (String) The redirect URI to register at an OIDC identity provider.
- `sp_entity_id` (String) The entity ID (audience) to register at a SAML identity provider.
- `sp_metadata_url` (String) The URL of PushWard's service provider metadata, which it serves once the connection is SAML.

<a id="nestedatt--oidc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `oidc`

Required:

- `client_id` (String) Changing it takes an owner.
- `issuer` (String) The issuer, an https URL; PushWard reads its discovery document when it is set or changed. Changing it takes an owner.

Optional:

- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) The client secret, kept in the state as configured. Left out, PushWard keeps the stored one.
- `client_secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The client secret, write-only: never in the plan or the state. Sent when the connection is created and when `client_secret_wo_version` changes. Needs Terraform 1.11 or newer.
- `client_secret_wo_version` (Number) Change it to send `client_secret_wo` again, such as after rolling the secret at the identity provider.


<a id="nestedatt--saml"></a>
### Nested Schema for `saml`

Optional:

- `idp_metadata_url` (String) An https URL PushWard reads the metadata from, once per change. Left out, and without `idp_metadata_xml`, it shows the URL the stored metadata was read from, if any.
- `idp_metadata_xml` (String) The metadata document, one EntityDescriptor (`file()` helps). PushWard does not return it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The connection belongs to the key's organization; import it with the
# organization id.
terraform import pushward_org_sso_connection.this 0a3c5e7f-1b2d-4c6e-8f0a-2b4d6f8a0c1e
```
